message.content:
### Killing **Visual Studio Code** (`code.exe`) from the Command Prompt (or PowerShell) | What you’re doing | Why it matters | |-------------------|----------------| | `taskkill` – Windows built‑in utility that terminates processes by name or PID. | Lets you force‑close VS Code when it’s hung, stuck, or you just want to restart it quickly without going through Task Manager. | --- #### Basic one‑liner ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F ``` * `/IM code.exe` – “Image Name” → target all running `code.exe` instances.
* `/F`       – Force termination (equivalent to *End Process*). If you only have one instance open this will close it immediately. --- #### Target a specific instance (by PID) 1. Find the PID first: ```cmd tasklist /FI "imagename eq code.exe" ``` 2. Kill that exact PID: ```cmd taskkill /PID 12345 /F ``` *(Replace `12345` with the actual number.)* --- #### Multiple commands at once Sometimes you may want to run several cleanup steps before killing VS Code: ```cmd del "%APPDATA%\Code\Cache\*" && taskkill /IM code.exe /F ``` This deletes the cache folder then forces VS Code to exit. --- #### Common gotchas & tips | Issue | Fix/Advice | |-------|------------| | **“Access denied” error** | Run CMD/Powershell as Administrator. | | **VS Code still stays alive after `/F`** | Some extensions spawn child processes; ensure those are closed too. Use `/T` to terminate entire tree:
`taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T`. | | **Multiple windows/tabs but same executable** | All tabs share the same `code.exe`; the above kills everything. If you need finer control, consider sending a graceful shutdown signal instead (see below). | | **PowerShell users** | Equivalent: `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | --- #### Graceful shutdown (recommended over forced kill) Instead of hard‑killing, let VS Code try to shut down cleanly: ```cmd tskill code ``` or in PowerShell: ```powershell Get-Process code | Stop-Process ``` These send a normal WM_CLOSE event so settings/extensions get saved properly. Only fall back to `taskkill /F` if the app truly hangs. --- #### Quick cheat sheet | Action | Cmd line | |--------|----------| | List all VS Code PIDs | `tasklist /FI "imagename eq code.exe"` | | Terminate all VS Code instances | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | | Terminate a particular PID | `taskkill /PID /F` | | Terminate + children | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` | | Graceful stop (no force) | `tskill code` or `Stop-Process -Name code` | That covers most scenarios where you’d want to kill VS Code programmatically. Happy coding!
